home.welcome.description: Rangers are some of the most essential workers on the planet. They protect and manage the world's protected and conserved areas — yet their contributions are often undervalued and their needs overlooked. The 11th World Ranger Congress brings together 600+ rangers and conservation professionals to change that.
home.iguazu.title: Puerto Iguazu Welcomes You…
home.iguazu.subtitle: 11th IRF WRC 2027
home.iguazu.p1: Nestled at the Triple Frontier where Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay converge, Puerto Iguazu is a gateway to one of the world's most spectacular natural wonders. The thundering Iguazu Falls, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, stands as a testament to the raw power and beauty of nature.
home.iguazu.p2: The surrounding Atlantic Forest is one of the most biodiverse regions on Earth, home to jaguars, toucans, coatis, and over 2,000 plant species. This extraordinary setting provides the perfect backdrop for the global ranger community to unite and advance conservation.

about.hero.title: About the Congress
about.hero.subtitle: Bringing together rangers and conservation professionals from around the world
about.intro.title: Rangers: Essential Workers for Our Planet
about.intro.p1: Rangers are some of the most essential workers on the planet. They protect and manage the world's protected and conserved areas, covering over 15% of the Earth's land surface and 8% of our oceans.
about.intro.p2: Yet their contributions are often undervalued, their working conditions poor, and their needs overlooked. The IRF World Ranger Congress is held in a different part of the world every 3-4 years, bringing together rangers to share experiences, build networks, and advance the profession.
about.wrc.title: About the 11th IRF World Ranger Congress
about.wrc.subtitle: Puerto Iguazu, Argentina · 19-23 April 2027
about.wrc.p1: For the first time, the World Ranger Congress comes to Argentina, set against the stunning backdrop of Iguazu Falls and the Atlantic Forest. This historic event marks a milestone for Latin American conservation and ranger communities.
about.wrc.p2: Puerto Iguazu sits at the Triple Frontier — where Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay meet — making it a symbol of international cooperation in conservation. The congress will produce the Iguazu Declaration, a landmark statement emphasizing the role of rangers in nature conservation.
about.wrc.p3: 600 delegates from over 50 countries will gather for five days of plenary talks, workshops, field trips, and cultural exchanges.
about.activities.title: Congress Activities
about.activities.plenaryDesc: Sessions by prominent conservation experts addressing inclusive workforce, welfare of rangers, conduct, and capacity building.
about.activities.workshopsDesc: Thematic workshops on equity & equality, indigenous people, one health, youth involvement, and more.
about.activities.discussionsDesc: Informal platforms for Indigenous Peoples, female rangers, youth leaders, volunteers, and retired rangers.
about.activities.culturalDesc: Evening entertainment featuring music, art, and cultural expressions from ranger communities worldwide.
about.activities.fieldTripsDesc: Excursions to Iguazu National Park, Devil's Throat walkways.
about.theme.title: Congress Theme
about.theme.quote: Recognising Rangers: Advancing the profession to safeguard our future
about.theme.description: The theme focuses on improving working conditions, providing better equipment and training, and empowering rangers to play their vital role in biodiversity protection and building a sustainable future.
about.objectives.title: Congress Objectives
about.objectives.recognitionDesc: Enhance recognition of the ranger profession and align with the global 30x30 Framework to protect 30% of the planet by 2030.
about.objectives.experiencesDesc: Showcase ranger experiences, challenges, and contributions from all seven IRF regions worldwide.
about.objectives.solutionsDesc: Develop practical solutions for regional and global conservation challenges through collaboration and knowledge sharing.
about.objectives.declarationDesc: Produce the Iguazu Declaration — a landmark statement emphasizing the role of rangers in nature conservation.

events.fieldTrips.title: Devil's Throat Walkways — Iguazu National Park
events.fieldTrips.description: On Monday 21 April, delegates will visit the Devil's Throat walkways at Iguazu Falls. The trail is approximately 2,200 metres round trip (about 2 hours), fully accessible via footbridges. Witness the massive river water plummeting into the gorge, creating a mist visible from over 7 kilometres away. Access is via the Ecological Train of the Jungle to the Garganta del Diablo Station.
